params.id: MUSCLE-1 successor M1b = M1 + the electrochemical delay (EMG → fascicle motion) on the excitation; nothing else changed

PF.src: FORCE_PRODUCTION_LITERATURE §12.2 plantarflexors: step-drive 10–90 % rise 250–450 ms (central 300–350) [E §9]; relaxation 90–10 % 120–250 ms (central ≈ 175) [E]; τc by cascade inversion on the 240 Hz discrete cascade (m1_design_derive.mjs) [E]

KF.src: [D] knee flexors: no step-drive or relaxation data (§10 gap); the knee-extensor values are borrowed (§12.2 'borrow knee-extensor structure with wider bounds')

params.stiffnessState: developed force f (not activation a) — Hunter & Kearney 1983; Kirsch & Rymer 1992 [M]: stiffness follows developed torque, not EMG
params.strainArms: force-based (incremental stiffness); detachment ∝ fall of developed force; attachment unstrained; persistent / slow / fast weights and time constants = S2's (fRes 0.15, wS 0.30 τ 0.5 s, wF 0.55 τ 20 ms), cap R⁺ + R⁻ from developed force

electrochemicalDelay.src: Nordez et al. 2009 (J Appl Physiol 106:1970, PMID 19359617) [M]: medial gastrocnemius fascicle-motion onset 6.05 ± 0.64 ms after EMG onset (evoked; the rest of the 11.6 ms EMD is series-elastic take-up, 47.5 %); FORCE_PRODUCTION_LITERATURE §12.2 "pure transport delay ≈ 6 ms". Rounded UP to whole 240 Hz steps (2 = 8.33 ms) by the project convention that no pathway is faster than in humans (PPR-3 POSTURAL_TIMING §delays). Applied to every muscle group (no muscle-specific data)
